power.title: Power Analysis Check

table.text: These mode-matched, not token-budget-matched, contrasts are in Supplementary Note S38. Physician safety ratings are inconclusive Three physicians rated seed-1 lists for all 34 top-1-discordant original-cohort cases. S1 danger (mean AC1 0•185), dangerous-omission (0•423/0•458), and D5 preference (0•196) missed the 0•6 agreement gate; only misleading-inclusion ratings met it (0•834/0•726). The safety comparison is therefore inconclusive. Descriptively, 23 of 34 majority verdicts were ties (non-tied 6:5; MDTmore-dangerous rate 0•545, 95% CI 0•234 to 0•833); omission flags favoured A×1 (26•5% versus 14•7%), misleading-inclusion flags MDT (0% versus 14•7%), but power covered only preferences beyond ~72% (Supplementary Figure S2d; Supplementary Note S37). On the replacement cohort the redesigned rating passed the gate for every family except D5 preference (mean AC1 0•836 danger, 0•819/0•992 omission/inclusion flags, 0•822 rescue; D5 0•467, descriptive), with perfect intra-rater agreement (14/14 embedded repeats each). The primary question-did the losing list contain an acceptable entry encompassing the reference? was answered yes for 29 of 35 team-lost cases (82•9%) and 18 of 18 single-call-lost cases (100%); the -17•1-point difference (95% Newcombe CI -32•7 to +2•6) leaves the forceddifferentiation mechanism neither validated nor refuted, in the direction opposite to the hypothesis (baseline rescue on concordant misses 6/15, 40%). The secondary danger comparison was null (MDT more dangerous in 3 of 11 non-tied units, p = 0•23; omission flags 8:3, p = 0•23; misleading inclusion 0:0; no side preference in controls) (Supplementary Note S39).

::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"}

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

> An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen's d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

> A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.

:::

text.text: Background.

Whether multi-agent large language model (LLM) pipelines help, add nothing, or underperform a single call may depend on the input and scoring contract rather than the architecture; these boundary conditions are unmapped.

We compared a single direct call (A×1), five personas in one context (P), and five isolated roles integrated by a moderator (MDT) across curated corpora (87 clinicopathological cases, 406 MedCaseReasoning cases, 392 replication vignettes) and two disjoint emergency cohorts from one repository (364 mixed-label encounters; a protocol-frozen 400-encounter disease-label-only replacement, one local serving stack).
Scoring was judge-mediated top-k working-label matching.
A completed factorial isolated the active ingredient; a symptompermissive output-contract arm tested contract fit; three physicians rated discordant cases.
Findings.

On curated corpora MDT improved differential-list recall (top-3: +5•5 points, p = 0•0079; +3•0, p = 0•0079; +3•3, p = 0•0013) but not top-1 accuracy; the factorial attributed the gain to independent generation plus moderated synthesis, not personas.

On emergency presentations the sign reversed: in the disease-label-only cohort A×1 led MDT at every endpoint (top-3 -5•2 points, 95% CI -8•0 to -2•4, p = 0•0008), a second family reproduced it, and bridged cases excluded the serving stack.
A symptom-permissive contract shrank the deficit's point estimates by 52-75%, replacement-cohort intervals all spanning zero though remaining negative; the clause harmed no arm.
Physician safety ratings were inconclusive (original-cohort gate missed; replacement-cohort rescue contrast unadjudicable, 95% CI -32•7 to +2•6).
Interpretation.
Multi-agent diagnostic gains are real but conditional: the sign of the effect tracks input genre, and its magnitude tracks output-contract fit.

Gains measured on curated benchmarks should not be extrapolated to first-contact clinical text.
Where multi-call designs are used on uncurated input, plain independent samples with a moderating call avoid the role-list penalty.
An output contract permitting undifferentiated symptom-level entries is free-it harmed no arm-and is a defensible default wherever reference labels may be working diagnoses.
Strategy selection by input, model, and endpoint remains a hypothesis requiring prospective evaluation, with independent emergency datasets and adequately powered safety studies.
extrapolated to first-contact emergency text, where role-based teams underperform a single call at seven-fold token cost.
The reversal is label-level and judge-mediated; clinical safety is neither established nor excluded.

text.text: Evidence before this study.

Multi-agent LLM diagnostic pipelines report gains, but specialist personas, independent generation, synthesis, and additional test-time compute are usually varied together, so the active ingredient is unidentified.

Evaluation is concentrated on curated case reports, leaving performance on first-contact notes and working-diagnosis labels unclear, and no study has tested whether the output contract demanded of the model contributes to measured underperformance.
Across curated corpora and two disjoint emergency cohorts, we show the multi-agent effect is conditional and map two of its moderators.
A completed factorial attributes the curated gain to independent generation plus moderated synthesis, not personas, and confines it to differential-list recall.

The emergency deficit is established on a protocol-frozen cohort whose labels are all disease-level diagnoses, reproduced by a second model family on the same cases, and insensitive to the serving stack on bridged cases-so neither symptom-level labels nor the stack explains it.
A symptom-permissive output contract closes the breadth component of the deficit while the ordering component persists.
Physician safety ratings are inconclusive by design.
Diagnostic error is a leading source of preventable harm [1, 2], and large language models (LLMs) now perform competitively on benchmarks built for expert diagnosticians [3, 4, 5, 6, 7].

text.text: Two issues remain entangled.

"Multiple perspectives" can mean personas voiced sequentially in one context or independent opinions combined afterwards, but these configurations also differ in calls, synthesis, and intermediate output structure.

In addition, evaluation concentrates on curated, information-rich case reports rather than emergency presentations, where input is incomplete and the reference is the treating clinician's working label.
We compared single-call, sequentialpersona, and moderated-team strategies across corpora differing in difficulty, provenance, and label structure.
Our primary contrasts were MDT-A×1 at top-3 and top-5.
We treated factorial and persona contrasts as secondary, emergency performance as judge-mediated working-label matching, and cross-corpus patterns as descriptive.

We compared three prompting strategies on datasets differing in difficulty, provenance, and label structure; all received the same case text and returned a ranked top-5 differential, scored against the reference diagnosis.
The development corpus was 87 CPC cases (2013-2016) [5], split into 41 prompt-design and 46 held-out.

In revision, a replacement primary cohort of 400 disease-label encounters was drawn from the same repository under a protocol frozen before any generation: all original-cohort cases excluded, every candidate label audited, fixed-seed chief-complaint-stratified sampling, identical prompts and temperatures, one local serving stack, five seeds (self-frozen protocol; Statistical analysis); the original-cohort analysis is retained unchanged (Supplementary Note S39).

To test whether additional information changed the emergency result, we appended each encounter's objective results to its presentation (prompts, model, decoding, seeds, judge unchanged); filters, leakage checks, and the label-in-text analysis are in Supplementary Methods S-M8.

To compare input forms on fixed content, we harvested full narrative case reports from PubMed Central and rewrote them into teaching vignettes under a condenser prompt forbidding disclosure of the reference diagnosis, with a zero-tolerance dual audit, an exploratory length-matched filler arm, and a protocol-frozen expansion to 392 replication vignettes; construction details and the selection-asymmetry disclosure are in the supplement (Supplementary Methods S-M6; Supplementary Note S35).
The primary CPC, MedCaseReasoning, and emergency comparisons used qwen3.8-flash (176B, provider-documented, thinking disabled) and returned a ranked top-5 list.

text.text: Output-contract fit tracks the magnitude: a safe one-sentence partial fix Because the strict contract demands disease-level entries while many emergency labels are working diagnoses, we tested a symptom-permissive contract-one appended sentence permitting undifferentiated entries over unsupported disease guesses (Methods; plan frozen before generation).
On the original cohort it closed the breadth end of the symptom-stratum deficit (top-5 -9•6 points, p = 0•0036, to -3•2, interval spanning zero) while the ordering end persisted.

On the fresh cohort, where every label is a disease diagnosis, the same contract narrowed the gap at every endpoint (point estimates shrinking 52-75%, all intervals spanning zero; gap shift +3•0 at top-5, p = 0•06): part of the reversal is an artefact of forced disease guessing under the strict contract on which the pre-specified primary result rests.
The clause was safe and selective: on the original cohort it added +6•4 top-5 points to MDT and +5•1 to P (both p  S3; Supplementary Tables S11, S17).

text.text: Whether a multi-agent team helped, added nothing, or underperformed depended on configuration, not architecture.
On curated corpora the moderated team improved the differential's breadth without robustly improving its head; the factorial attributed the gain to independent generation plus moderated synthesis.

On uncurated emergency presentations the sign reversed-persisting with all disease-level labels, in a second model family, and across serving stacks-and multi-call inference is not the cause: five plain samples under the same moderator matched the single call while the role-based team sat 6•8 points below it at top-3.
Two moderators organise this heterogeneity.
Input genre: the margin ran from positive on curated vignettes through null on self-disclosing narratives to negative on uncurated emergency text, the within-case contrast pointing the same way.

Output-contract fit is the actionable moderator: a one-sentence clause permitting undifferentiated entries closed the breadth component of the emergency deficit (halving point estimates even where every label was a disease diagnosis), the ordering component persisting.

Two strictnesses must be distinguished: scoring strictness fell on both arms and explains the gap in neither direction; contract strictness was not arm-neutral-the clause preferentially restored the team's recall (+4 to +5 versus +1 to +2 points), the signature of a dispersed candidate list forced to guess beyond the evidence.

The reversal is therefore partly an artefact of forced differentiation and partly a genuine ordering deficit; the frozen-protocol primary result rests on the strict contract shared with the other corpora.
The safety evidence, inconclusive on both cohorts, establishes neither clinical equivalence nor that the reversal is merely artefactual.

These results reconcile mixed literature: positive studies generated contributions separately and aggregated them [8, 13]; negative studies voiced personas in one context [14] or debated without feedback [15]; reports of models beating physicians on emergency cases used complete records and a comprehensiveness score that rewarded inclusion without penalising irrelevance [27], unlike our first-contact working-label design.

text.text: Collaboration benefits vary with capability and reasoning configuration [22, 23]; agent count and persona framing show no uniform effect across clinical tasks [17, 18, 24].
text.formatted: Collaboration benefits vary with capability and reasoning configuration <ref type="bibr" target="#b22">[22,</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b23">23]</ref>; agent count and persona framing show no uniform effect across clinical tasks <ref type="bibr" target="#b17">[17,</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b18">18,</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b24">24]</ref>.

text.text: Curated-benchmark gains should not be extrapolated to first-contact clinical input-the one setting whose labels no model could have memorised.

On uncurated input, plain independent samples with a moderating call are the defensible multi-call form, and a contract permitting undifferentiated entries is a defensible default wherever labels may be working diagnoses.

Strategy selection by input, model, endpoint, and reasoning mode remains a routing hypothesis for prospective evaluation; and because the reversal is label-level, judge-mediated, and clinically unadjudicated, these results argue for caution about deployment claims, not clinical harm.
Several limitations bound inference.
The primary emergency input stops before objective results, and the workup condition added objective content only; findings do not extend to complete-chart reasoning.

Both emergency cohorts come from one repository, use working diagnoses, and were scored by an imperfect judge-the replacement cohort removes label granularity but shares repository, working-label construct, and judge, whose clinician-validated κ on the new candidate distribution (0•54-0•56 against clinician-clinician 0•85) matches the original, leaving the reversal resting partly on a noisy instrument (Note S39).

The second-family result is same-cases model replication, not external validation; the same-rule second judge is a sensitivity analysis, not independent clinical validation; and the annotation samples support no unbiased arm-specific false-accept/false-reject estimates.

Both physician ratings were inconclusive: the original-cohort danger, omission, and preference families missed the agreement gate, and the replacement-cohort rescue contrast was unadjudicable (95% CI -32•7 to +2•6 points; power limited to ~35-40-point differences; D5 descriptive; 8 of 83 Part A units with a pre-declared seed-1 display deviation).

In the original cohort the deficit was directionally present in both label strata but separable only in the symptom stratum (top-3 and top-5 q = 0•049 and 0•022), and its magnitude was servingstack-sensitive (top-3 -9•0 cloud to -6•4 self-hosted, 4-bit quantisation a candidate explanation), though bridged cases bounded the stack contribution (50 cases, one seed; Note S39).
The outputcontract arm was added after the primary analyses under a pre-generation frozen plan, and its fresh-cohort intervals all span zero.
Clinician judge assessment did not cover the closed-model arms; part of the condensed-corpus adjudication used an alternative endpoint (94•99% agreement after equivalence checking).
Curated-corpus contamination and strategy-by-memorisation interactions cannot be excluded.
Cross-corpus contrasts confound model, deployment, labels, provenance, and contamination.
Analyses were not externally registered, and thinking arms were post hoc, excluded the emergency corpus, and yielded corpus-specific results.

Consistent with PhysioNet's guidance on credentialed data and large language models, all automated processing of these de-identified records met the guidance's conditions for acceptable automated processing: the emergencycorpus arms ran on self-hosted infrastructure with no transmission of case content off the machine, and the one replication that sent case text to a cloud provider used a zero-data-retention endpoint (no retention, no training use, no human review of case content), with the serving provider logged and audited on every request.
An amendment documenting this processing pathway was approved by the data provider's credentialing committee before the replication ran.

The physician rating component involved three practising clinicians assessing anonymised diagnosis lists derived from the same de-identified corpora on a local server, with no patient involvement and no case content leaving the rating environment; it is covered by the same exemption (No.

Before strategy comparison, the judge was assessed against two blinded clinicians on 100 development-untouched pairs (judge-clinician κ 0•814/0•878; inter-rater 0•812), with extension to other corpora (emergency symptom-level labels: inter-rater 0•612, judge-clinician 0•640/0•580; boundary-enriched rerun: 0•877, 0•580/0•540).
The same design on the fresh cohort reproduced these values (0•560/0•540; 0•849), leaving measured judge reliability unchanged for the replacement analysis.

Residual discordance was directional: clinicians endorsed 20 of 50 pairs the judge rejected but rejected only 3 of 50 it accepted, mostly concurrent or aetiologic candidates encompassing the reference; a full-corpus check found reference-containing false rejects running against the single call (8•8% vs 3•4%, p = 0•012), biasing the gap toward the null (Supplementary Tables

The original P arm scored below A×1 on CPC at every endpoint without significance; against Pfixed, MDT's CPC advantages were likewise non-significant (top-3 6•0, p = 0•0599; top-5 4•6, p = 0•0676), on MedCaseReasoning borderline at top-3 (+2•4, p = 0•0501) and significant at top-5 (+3•6, p = 0•0007).

text.text: Independent generation plus moderated synthesis, not personas, carries the curated gain In the completed factorial (Figure 3a), mechanical aggregation never helped: Borda over five single-call samples scored 9•5 points below A×1 on MedCaseReasoning top-1, and reaggregating team lists did not help either.

The same moderator over plain independent samples (A×5+Mod) recovered the advantage and matched the role-based team; A×1+CoT changed nothing (all p ≥0•61) and A×5 did not reproduce MDT (all p ≤0•059).
With the moderatoranatomy controls, the pattern is consistent with independent generation plus moderated synthesis.
On emergency text, plain samples plus a moderator exceeded MDT by 6•8 points at top-3 and 7•0 at top-5 without differing from A×1 (appendix).

On emergency presentations the effect reverses-and survives three stress tests On the protocol-frozen 400-case emergency cohort whose reference labels are all disease-level diagnoses (Methods), A×1 outperformed MDT at every endpoint: top-1 51•7% versus 47•2% (-4•5 points, 95% CI -7•8 to -1•3, p = 0•016), top-3 -5•2 (-8•0 to -2•4, p = 0•0008), top-5 -4•0 (-6•7 to -1•5, p = 0•0086); majority-vote McNemar concordant, all three surviving in-family correction (adjusted p 0•0159, 0•0024, 0•0129).
P also trailed A×1 on recall (top-3 -3•8, p = 0•047; top-5 -3•9, p = 0•021) and MDT added nothing over P, reproducing A×1 > P ≥ MDT at 7•3 times the single call's token cost.
text.formatted: P also trailed A×1 on recall (top-3 -3•8, p = 0•047; top-5 -3•9, p = 0•021) and MDT added nothing over P, reproducing A×1 > P ≥ MDT at 7•3 times the single call's token cost.

text.text: On 50 bridged original-cohort cases the MDT-A×1 estimate shifted within noise (top-3 +2•0, top-5 +6•0, intervals spanning zero; both stacks negative), so the reversal is not a stack artefact and does not rest on symptom-level labels (Supplementary Note S39).

The original-cohort analysis (364 encounters, two stacks, 46% symptom-level labels) is retained in full: A×1 beat MDT at every endpoint (top-1 -3•9, p = 0•021; top-3 -6•4, p = 0•0022; top-5 -6•4, p = 0•0039) and in temperature-matched and judge-independent word-coverage checks (37•3% versus 33•0% P, 30•8% MDT; Supplementary Figure S2b)-lexical coverage being no clinical correctness measure (Supplementary Table 360 points, 95% CI -8•256 to -0•464, p = 0•0322).

On the fresh cohort the workup gain replicated for every strategy (+5•9 to +7•8, p ≤ 0•0002) and the reversal persisted (top-3 -4•9, p = 0•0031), but the interaction was null at every endpoint: the original cohort's negative interaction did not replicate (Note S39).

Input genre tracks the sign of the effect (a descriptive map) Across corpora, MDT-A×1 top-3 point estimates ran +5•5 (CPC), +3•0 (MedCaseReasoning), +2•831 (condensed PMC vignettes, p = 0•0282), +1•108 (full PMC reports, p = 0•2134), and -6•4 (emergency notes) (Figure 4a).
On the same 325 reports the paired condensed-minus-full interaction was +1•723 points (p = 0•2393) and the exploratory single-seed filler arm +3•1 (p = 0•096).
The pooled 392-vignette replication cohort gave top-3 +3•3 (95% CI 1•5 to 5•1, p = 0•0013).

text.text: These mode-matched, not token-budget-matched, contrasts are in Supplementary Note S38.
Physician safety ratings are inconclusive Three physicians rated seed-1 lists for all 34 top-1-discordant original-cohort cases.
S1 danger (mean AC1 0•185), dangerous-omission (0•423/0•458), and D5 preference (0•196) missed the 0•6 agreement gate; only misleading-inclusion ratings met it (0•834/0•726).
The safety comparison is therefore inconclusive.

Descriptively, 23 of 34 majority verdicts were ties (non-tied 6:5; MDTmore-dangerous rate 0•545, 95% CI 0•234 to 0•833); omission flags favoured A×1 (26•5% versus 14•7%), misleading-inclusion flags MDT (0% versus 14•7%), but power covered only preferences beyond ~72% (Supplementary Figure S2d; Supplementary Note S37).

On the replacement cohort the redesigned rating passed the gate for every family except D5 preference (mean AC1 0•836 danger, 0•819/0•992 omission/inclusion flags, 0•822 rescue; D5 0•467, descriptive), with perfect intra-rater agreement (14/14 embedded repeats each).
The primary question-did the losing list contain an acceptable entry encompassing the reference?

was answered yes for 29 of 35 team-lost cases (82•9%) and 18 of 18 single-call-lost cases (100%); the -17•1-point difference (95% Newcombe CI -32•7 to +2•6) leaves the forceddifferentiation mechanism neither validated nor refuted, in the direction opposite to the hypothesis (baseline rescue on concordant misses 6/15, 40%).

The secondary danger comparison was null (MDT more dangerous in 3 of 11 non-tied units, p = 0•23; omission flags 8:3, p = 0•23; misleading inclusion 0:0; no side preference in controls) (Supplementary Note S39).
